    Counting in C(D) #

    Morphism spaces of C(D) have at most countable dimension when every D_i does: between single objects they are k, D_i, 0, or a morphism space between interval representations, of dimension at most one, and Hom(M, N) is the finite product of the spaces between the entries. Every indecomposable is isomorphic to a single object, so it has endomorphism ring k and the extension spaces between indecomposables have dimension at most one by (4.1); the isomorphism classes of indecomposables are in bijection with the labels X, Y, A i, P i.
